extracted.intended_audience: supporters, donors, journalists, and the general public interested in criminal justice reporting and reform
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and values describing how a nonprofit news organization (The Marshall Project) conducts and measures its criminal-justice reporting — emphasizing impact, nonpartisanship, accuracy, fairness, diversity, and collaboration with local media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: create and sustain national urgency about the criminal justice system
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization 'seeks to create and sustain a sense of national urgency about the U.S. criminal justice system.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use journalism to elevate criminal justice to a national priority and spark public conversation about reform; aim for reporting that moves attention and resources toward systemic problems rather than letting the issue fade from public consciousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpartisan reporting (not advocacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Marshall Project describes itself as 'a nonpartisan, nonprofit news organization' and says 'Although we are not advocates, The Marshall Project often spurs change.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain independence from partisan advocacy while pursuing reporting that can lead to reform; consciously avoid ideological selection of facts. The page explicitly notes 'Being nonpartisan is not the same as being neutral.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful, accurate, and honest journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: 'We believe that journalism, done honestly and well, has infinite power to drive change.' The organization emphasizes 'truthful story-telling' and 'factual reporting.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize factual accuracy even when reporting is disturbing; avoid selective presentation of facts; aim for reporting that can be relied upon by experts, officials, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact-driven journalism: expose wrongs and spur change
rubrics_metrics.description: The Marshall Project seeks to have an impact on the system 'through journalism, rendering it more fair, effective, transparent and humane.' It 'exposes wrongs, bringing them to the attention of officials who can take action' and 'spurs change.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue investigations and storytelling that can lead to concrete policy or practice changes. Examples cited include investigations prompting a prison unit shutdown, guilty pleas by guards after reporting, and municipal policy changes after a series on police dog bites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair and responsible coverage of criminal justice issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization aims 'to cover criminal justice issues fairly and responsibly' and to 'explore what is working as well as what is broken.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance critique with reporting on successful practices and reform opportunities; avoid sensationalism and aim for context that fairly represents all relevant perspectives and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve and engage people directly affected by the system
rubrics_metrics.description: The Marshall Project aims 'to serve and engage the millions of people whose lives have been ensnared in the criminal justice system, and whom the media have too often neglected and marginalized.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center reporting on the experiences and needs of incarcerated people, their families, and other marginalized populations; ensure coverage gives voice and visibility to those affected rather than only institutional actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, equity and inclusion in staffing and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization is 'committed to building and retaining a diverse staff and board, who bring a variety of experiences and perspectives to bear on the issues we cover.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit and retain staff and board members with diverse backgrounds and perspectives; report publicly on diversity work (e.g., an annual diversity report) and use diverse perspectives to inform editorial choices and coverage priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate with local and national media to reach diverse audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Marshall Project 'partners with both national and local media outlets to reach diverse audiences' and may 'open up offices in cities where there is a desperate need for high-quality criminal justice journalism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use partnerships and local presence to amplify reporting, fill local reporting gaps, and increase accountability in communities lacking newsrooms; tailor outreach and distribution to reach affected communities and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and watchdog emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization's reporting focuses on problems in police, courts and prisons (e.g., racial and economic inequities, violence, solitary confinement) and aims to hold institutions accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct investigations that reveal institutional failures and abuses, providing evidence that can be used by officials, advocates, and the public to demand change; include concrete examples of institutional harms and remedies where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial excellence and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Founding and current editors assembled 'a first-class team of reporters and editors dedicated to excellence, nonpartisan reporting, and innovation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in high-quality reporting and editorial standards, experiment with innovative storytelling or distribution methods, and uphold rigorous newsroom practices to produce trustworthy, influential journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical transparency and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: The site references a 'Code of Ethics,' 'Privacy Policy,' and 'Advertising Policy' as part of its organizational framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear, publicly available ethical and policy documents governing editorial conduct, privacy, and advertising to preserve editorial independence and public trust; use policies to guide conflicts of interest and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of historical context and contemporary analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The page situates present-day criminal justice issues within historical developments (e.g., references to 'The New Jim Crow,' Thurgood Marshall, and historical legal milestones) to explain systemic causes and impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate historical context and scholarship into reporting to help audiences understand systemic roots and long-term patterns, not just isolated incidents; cite authoritative works and historical cases where relevant.
